solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; the grid proves the blog's enumeration wrong at 4 down, recounted from the answer here

clue.text: Desire dealing with Hades?

indicators.note: dealing, as with a pack of cards, mixes up the letters of with Hades

explanation.surface: A question about some craving connected with the Greek underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dealing with' reads as 'concerning', but 'dealing' is the anagram signal and WITH HADES is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A longing for one's own end is a kind of desire, the psychological term for a drive towards dying.

clue.text: Surrey town has queen and king go visiting as a tourist

indicators.note: go means the royal letters depart from the town's name

parts.note: Dorking is a market town in Surrey, a county south of London
R is short for regina, queen
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A Surrey town where the royal couple go sightseeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' removes R and K from DORKING; DORKING is a town in Surrey, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourists say they are doing Paris or Rome when touring its sights, an informal idiom.

clue.text: Former standard ministry test covering local spirit in Rome's ruins?

parts.note: ancient is an old word for a flag or ensign, a standard

indicators.note: covering means the test's letters go around the spirit

parts.note: the MOT is the annual UK roadworthiness test, named after the Ministry of Transport
a numen is the presiding spirit of a place in Roman religion

explanation.surface: An old flag and a government inspection somehow cover a Roman genius loci among the ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: MOT is Britain's annual car safety check; 'ancient' as a flag is archaic, as in Shakespeare's Pistol.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruined Roman buildings are examples of protected historic structures; the question mark marks Rome's ruins as one instance.

clue.text: Teacher is embraced by heterosexual bon vivant

indicators.note: embraced by means the teacher and is sit inside the heterosexual word

parts.note: het is informal shorthand for heterosexual
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A pleasure-loving teacher is hugged by a straight man.
explanation.definitionFit: A bon vivant lives for pleasure and good food, exactly the pleasure-seeker type.

clue.text: People in the north losing fine pubs

indicators.note: losing means the fine letter is dropped from the people's name

parts.note: Finns are the people of Finland in northern Europe
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Northerners fined and losing their local bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Taverns and public houses are both everyday names for places serving drink.

clue.text: Prime minister with bluff character in novel

parts.note: Edward Heath was British Prime Minister from 1970 to 1974
a bluff is a steep cliff or headland

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister paired with a gruff figure from fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bluff' looks like a personality word but is a headland. Heath was a British Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The brooding hero of Emily Brontë's Wuthering Heights is a famous fictional figure.

clue.text: Scratch twit regularly? These will do

definitions.text: Scratch twit regularly? These will do

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words Scratch twit, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Wondering who will keep on scratching a fool, the answer being spiny plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of SCRATCH TWIT; the whole clue is also the definition, since spiny desert plants will scratch anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiny succulents are covered in prickles that will scratch anyone who brushes against them.

clue.text: Reluctant to talk about medical farce, perhaps

indicators.note: about means the reticent word goes around the medical letters

parts.note: coy means shy and reticent

explanation.surface: A medical farce where someone is unwilling to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Farce is one example of the humorous drama genre, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Pass on bread mixed with my fries?

parts.note: bread is slang for money, cash
in can mean mixed with, as an ingredient added in
one's is the impersonal way of saying my
chips is British for fries

explanation.surface: Someone passing on a bread roll in favour of chips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass on' looks like declining food but means to die.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are euphemistic idioms for dying, the gambler's version settling one's account.

clue.text: Cite hefty changes as a reason for leaving?

indicators.note: changes means the letters of cite hefty are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone citing big changes as why they quit their job.
explanation.definitionFit: Restlessness and the urge to travel are an idiom for wanting to move on, a motive for departing.

clue.text: Score during period of play

parts.note: a score here is written music, and this kind accompanies a stage play while it runs

explanation.surface: Reads like a sports report of a goal scored while the game was on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' and 'play' suggest a match, but the score is a composer's and the play is theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Background music written to accompany a theatrical production is the composer's score heard during the performance.

clue.text: Signs people should go for vegetables

definitions.meaning: traffic lights showing the colour that means proceed
leafy vegetables such as cabbage and spinach, as a plural noun

explanation.surface: Signs that it is time to go and buy vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: The go colour on traffic lights, and in the plural the everyday word for leafy cooked vegetables.

clue.text: Carelessly wearing horseshoes daily? Not the answer

parts.note: a horse wearing horseshoes is said to be shod

indicators.note: Not means the letter standing for the answer is left out of the word daily

parts.note: A is the standard abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A horse carelessly shod every day, and a hint that the solution is something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not the answer' looks like a comment on the clue, but it removes A (answer) from DAILY to leave DILY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a shabby, badly made way means doing it without care.

clue.text: Wrongly copy Martin O'Leary, perhaps?

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters of copy Martin are set out in an incorrect order

explanation.surface: Someone has wrongly copied out a person's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish O' prefix means descendant of, so O'Leary is a family name derived from an ancestor's name.

clue.text: Fairly resistant to upsetting food after meat's off

indicators.note: after puts the food after the rearranged letters
meat that has gone off is spoiled, so its letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the letters of meat plus the S of the possessive
table can mean the food served, as in keeping a good table

explanation.surface: A queasy diner, fairly hardy, can stomach food after the meat has gone bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fairly resistant to upsetting' is a physics definition; table here is the old sense of food set out, as in keeping a good table.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics a state that is stable against small disturbances but not large ones is described with this term.

clue.text: Gas used in white wine plant

indicators.note: used in means the talking word is put inside the wine

parts.note: Mosel is a German white wine from the Moselle valley
to gas is to chat idly

explanation.surface: A gas employed in making white wine from a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A small woodland flower also called town-hall clock is a botanical species, so a plant.

clue.text: Girl's keeping new belt

indicators.note: keeping means the girl's name holds the other letter inside it

parts.note: Zoe is a girl's name; the 's is a link meaning has

explanation.surface: A girl holding on to her new belt.
explanation.definitionFit: A belt in geography is a region or area, such as a commuter belt or a time area.

clue.text: Bear with wild cat killing ten in New York area

parts.note: to brook is to bear or tolerate

indicators.note: killing means the ten letter is wiped out from the cat

parts.note: a lynx is a wild cat
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: A bear and a wild cat killing ten people in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal beside the wild cat, but it is the verb to tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: The borough across the East River from Manhattan is one of the five districts of the city.

clue.text: Hard entering pig as exhibit

indicators.note: entering means the hard letter goes into the word for the pig

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A tough pig shown off as an exhibit at a fair.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhibit something is to display or present it publicly.

clue.text: What gay chap will do tango a step ahead?

parts.note: a gay man will favour men, that is prefer men
Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dance-floor quip about a gay man taking the lead in the tango.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a step ahead' sounds like dance talk but is the definition: being moved up a rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Promotion to a higher office or rank puts someone a step up the ladder.

clue.text: Walk in street and trip

parts.note: a ride is a trip or journey

explanation.surface: Walking in the street and stumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' suggests stumbling but is a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A long purposeful step, and the verb for walking with such steps.

clue.text: Searching outside area in pursuit of ghosts

indicators.note: outside means the searching word sits around the area letter

parts.note: searching for something is hunting for it

explanation.surface: Searching an area while chasing spectres.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectres traditionally visit and frequent a place, and that activity is what ghosts pursue.

clue.text: Agree to deceive copper, right

parts.note: to con someone is to deceive them
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Agreeing to swindle a policeman, which is right.
explanation.definitionFit: To be of the same opinion as someone else is to agree with them.

clue.text: Low energy holds back what regeneration will do

indicators.note: back means the held letters are read in reverse
holds means the letters are held within the words Low energy

explanation.surface: Weak energy is held up by whatever will regenerate it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' and 'back' together: the letters run backwards inside lOW ENERgy.
explanation.definitionFit: Regenerating something restores or revives it, making it fresh again.

clue.text: Raised French meat as farm produce

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is lifted to read upwards

parts.note: porc is French for pork

explanation.surface: French livestock raised for meat sold as farm produce.
explanation.definitionFit: A harvest of grain or vegetables is the yield a farm produces.

clue.text: Epic fantasy gets millionth serial broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of millionth serial are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: An epic fantasy earns a record for its millionth radio episode.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien's posthumously published mythology of Middle-earth is an epic work of fantasy.

clue.text: Coffee time's interrupted recently

indicators.note: interrupted means the word for recently is broken into by the time letter

parts.note: late can mean recently, as in of late

explanation.surface: A coffee break whose time has lately been cut into.
explanation.definitionFit: A milky espresso drink is one of the standard coffees on any café menu.

clue.text: Surviving a lot of wash capsizing cutter

parts.note: coping means managing or getting by, surviving

indicators.note: capsizing in a down clue turns the letters upside down, read from the bottom up
a lot of means most of the word wash, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A cutter boat survives most of a wave's wash as it capsizes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' takes WAS from WASH; 'capsizing' reverses it to SAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine-bladed saw for cutting curves is a tool that cuts, so cutter is a general term for it.
